instruction: In Thunderbird, go to the Bills folder, choose the latest email, and open its primary link in Chrome as the focused tab.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the latest email in Thunderbird's Bills folder and opening the first URL (https://www.amazon.com/) in Chrome. The evaluator verifies that the active tab's URL is https://www.amazon.com/ using the existing is_expected_active_tab metric function. This reuses existing evaluator functions without requiring custom code.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts active tab state using get_active_tab_info (chrome.py:781-868), which retrieves URL from accessibility tree and connects to Chrome via CDP
Metric logic correctly compares URLs using is_expected_active_tab (chrome.py:18-38) with proper parameter handling - receives rules dict directly and accesses rule['type'] and rule['url']
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the final requirement that the correct URL (https://www.amazon.com/) is open in Chrome's active tab
Expected value is correct: https://www.amazon.com/ matches the first URL from the Bills folder email as stated in metadata
Data flow is correct: getter returns {title, url, content} → metric receives active_tab_info and rule dict → compares URLs using compare_urls utility → returns 1.0 for match
No parameter handling antipatterns: metric correctly uses 'rule' parameter name and accesses rule['url'] directly without incorrect patterns like expected.get('rules')
State timing is appropriate: getter reads active tab state after task completion, no postconfig needed
